fields.field: C-<date>-<nnn>. The contract id; a promise points at it via <contract ref="…">.

open = drafted, not yet ratified; ratified = accepted before code (the only state work may start against); broken = a check falsified mid-build; renegotiated = superseded by a new version via the originator (a worker cannot amend its own — §contracts-before-code).
The falsifiable definition of done, embed="true". What must be true, not how.

One acceptance check; repeatable. Attributes: id, assessor. Children: optional <run> (the command — its exit code is the verdict, 0=PASS), required <expect> (the outcome the assessor compares against). A check with a <run> is auto-verifiable; one without is MANUAL.
What this contract deliberately does NOT cover, embed="true" — bounds the promise.
What must keep working, embed="true" — the blast radius a fix must not break.

contract.goal: `socom contract verify` runs a contract's checks and exits nonzero iff an auto check fails; manual checks are reported, never auto-passed.

check.expect: exit 0 — the auto check passes and is reported PASS
verify prints this as MANUAL with assessor=reviewer; never auto-passed

contract.out-of-scope: Comparing a check's live output against the prose <expect> — verify runs the command and judges on exit code; the assessor reads the rest.
contract.regression-surface: A contract embedded in a promise must verify identically to a standalone one.
